mainTopic: Sources for inheritance rules: why a son comes before a daughter, why brothers inherit only through the father's side, and the start of the source for a son inheriting his mother.
overview: This amud looks for the source that a son comes before a daughter in inheritance. אביי says it comes from the words 'וּבֵן אֵין לוֹ' (and he has no son). He knocks down רב פפא's idea that a son and daughter would split the estate equally, since then the פסוק would be teaching something obvious. Two other sources are tried and rejected: רב אחא בר יעקב's proof from the words of בנות צלפחד, and רבינא's proof from 'הַקָּרֹב אֵלָיו'. Each time the גמרא goes back to the first source. Another source is offered from 'לִבְנֵיכֶם', and it survives a challenge because a בְּרָכָה is read differently from a law. The גמרא then asks how we know that brothers from the same father inherit from each other. It concludes that the word משפחה already teaches that inheritance goes through the father's side, and רבה's comparison to the sons of יעקב is really about יבום. Finally, the גמרא asks for the source that a man inherits his mother and begins a ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If neither child wins, who inherits?
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב פפא: if a son and daughter both exist and neither comes first, who is supposed to inherit? The city governor?
steps.simpleTranslation: Who then should inherit? Are you saying the governor of the city should inherit?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי mocks רב פפא's suggestion that when there is both a son and a daughter, 'neither one' gets priority. Somebody has to inherit, so that reading seems to leave no heir.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא had said that when both a son and a daughter exist, neither one comes first. אביי takes this to mean that neither one inherits, which would be absurd, as if a stranger like the city governor should take the estate. The challenge pushes רב פפא to explain what he really meant.

keyTerms.meaning: should inherit
Is that to say...? (an outraged question)
the ruler or governor of the city

phrases.english: Who, etc., should inherit?
Is that to say the ruler of the city should inherit?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the debate from before this section, where רב פפא suggested an alternate reading of 'וּבֵן אֵין לוֹ'.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's reading that when both a son and a daughter exist, 'neither' one takes precedence.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reductio ad absurdum: if neither one inherits, the estate would be left with no heir. That cannot be right.

steps.title: Son and daughter split equally
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains: I did not mean neither one inherits. I meant neither one takes everything, so they split it equally.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what I meant: if there is a son and a daughter, this one does not inherit all of it and that one does not inherit all of it. Rather, they inherit equally with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא clears up his words. 'Neither one' means neither child takes the whole estate. They share it equally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The absurd picture of no heir at all goes away. Under רב פפא's reading, the פסוק 'וּבֵן אֵין לוֹ' tells us only that a daughter inherits when there is no son. It does not tell us that a son pushes a daughter out.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what I meant to say
equally, like one another

phrases.english: This is what I meant to say:
If there is a son and a daughter,
this one should not inherit all of it,
and that one should not inherit all of it,
rather, they should inherit equally with each other!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge by clarifying what 'neither' meant.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי understood that neither the son nor the daughter would inherit at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Neither one takes the whole estate. Son and daughter share equally.

steps.title: Why would the Torah teach the obvious?
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects: under your reading, the פסוק only teaches that an only child inherits everything. Why would we need a פסוק for that?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Is a פסוק needed to teach us that when someone has only one child, that child inherits all the property?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב פפא's reading. If son and daughter are equal, the פסוק would be teaching something obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a daughter is just as strong an heir as a son, then 'when there is no son, the daughter inherits' only means 'a lone child takes everything.' Nobody needs a פסוק to know that. So the words 'וּבֵן אֵין לוֹ' must be teaching that a son comes first.

keyTerms.meaning: is a פסוק needed?
to teach us
one child
property, estate

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
And is a verse needed to teach us

phrases.aramaic: הֵיכָא דְּלֵית לֵיהּ אֶלָּא חַד בְּרָא,
phrases.english: that where he has only one child,
that child should inherit all the property?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the clarified position from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's reading of 'וּבֵן אֵין לוֹ' as giving the son no priority.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that reading the פסוק would be teaching something obvious, so the reading must be wrong.

steps.title: Maybe the פסוק teaches that daughters can inherit
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא suggests the פסוק is still needed: it teaches that a daughter can be an heir at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps this is what it teaches us: that a daughter is also someone who can inherit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends his reading by giving the פסוק a new job. It shows that a daughter is a legal heir.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we did not already know daughters could inherit, the פסוק would not be teaching the obvious. Then it would not need to be teaching that a son comes first. This saves רב פפא's reading only if no other source teaches this point.

keyTerms.meaning: and perhaps
this is what it teaches us
someone who can inherit

phrases.english: And perhaps this is what it teaches us:
that a daughter, too, is someone who can inherit?
phrases.notes: This is רב פפא speaking again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to אביי's 'the פסוק is unnecessary' challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Giving the פסוק a different purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק would be useless under רב פפא's reading.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק is needed to establish that daughters are heirs at all.

steps.title: That point comes from a different פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב פפא's defense. A different פסוק already teaches that a daughter can inherit.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is learned from 'And every daughter who inherits a portion.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shuts down רב פפא's defense. We already know daughters can inherit from another פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'וְכׇל בַּת יֹרֶשֶׁת נַחֲלָה' already shows a daughter can inherit, 'וּבֵן אֵין לוֹ' cannot be needed for that. So אביי's point stands: the words 'וּבֵן אֵין לוֹ' teach that a son comes first.

keyTerms.meaning: and every daughter who inherits a portion (במדבר 36:8)
is derived, comes out from

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's source stands: the פסוק 'וּבֵן אֵין לוֹ' teaches that a son comes before a daughter. The fact that daughters can inherit at all comes from a different פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא מִ״וְּכׇל בַּת יֹרֶשֶׁת נַחֲלָה״ נָפְקָא.
phrases.english: That is derived from 'And every daughter who inherits a portion.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא מִוְּכׇל בַּת יֹרֶשֶׁת נַחֲלָה נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the defense offered in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב פפא's claim that 'וּבֵן אֵין לוֹ' is needed to teach that daughters inherit.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That lesson is already taught by another פסוק, so it cannot be the purpose here.

steps.title: Another source from the daughters' own words
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב brings a different source: the daughters of צלפחד asked to inherit only because their father 'has no son.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: from here: 'Why should our father's name be lost from his family because he has no son?' The reason they could ask is that he had no son. But if he had a son, the son comes first.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא offers another source that a son comes before a daughter. He learns it from the request of בנות צלפחד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The daughters based their claim on the fact that their father had no son. So if there had been a son, he would have come first. This learns the rule from what the daughters said, not from what the תורה commanded.

keyTerms.meaning: from here
be diminished, be lost
the reason is
comes first

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר, מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov said: from here:
'Why should the name of our father be lost
phrases.notes: במדבר 27:4. These are the words of בנות צלפחד to משה.

phrases.aramaic: מִתּוֹךְ מִשְׁפַּחְתּוֹ, כִּי אֵין לוֹ בֵּן״.
phrases.english: from among his family, because he has no son?'
The reason is that he has no son;

phrases.aramaic: הָא יֵשׁ לוֹ בֵּן – בֵּן קוֹדֵם.
phrases.english: but if he has a son, the son comes first.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר, מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source for the same rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A son comes before a daughter in inheritance, learned from the daughters' words 'כִּי אֵין לוֹ בֵּן'.

steps.title: Maybe the daughters spoke before the new law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אחא בר יעקב: that was only what the daughters thought. The תורה may then have given a new law.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it was the daughters of צלפחד who said this, and then the Torah was given and a new law began.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes a hole in רב אחא בר יעקב's source. The daughters' words show only what they believed, not what the תורה then ruled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The daughters spoke before ה׳ answered משה. Maybe they were following the custom of their time. The תורה's answer could have brought a new rule, such as equal shares for sons and daughters. So their words cannot prove the final law.

keyTerms.meaning: the daughters of צלפחד
the Torah was given (here: ה׳'s answer to משה)
a new law was started

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up what בנות צלפחד said with what ה׳ answered. The question here is whether the daughters' assumption can count as the Torah's law.

phrases.english: But perhaps it was the daughters of Zelophehad
who said this;
then the Torah was given, and a new law began!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא בְּנוֹת צְלָפְחָד הוּא דְּקָאָמְרָן הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אחא בר יעקב's source.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using the daughters' words as proof of the law.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their words show only what they assumed before ה׳ answered. The Torah's answer could have set a new law.

steps.title: Back to the first source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the challenge and goes back to the first source, 'וּבֵן אֵין לוֹ'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear that the source is as we answered at first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops רב אחא בר יעקב's source. It goes back to the first one, אביי's reading of 'וּבֵן אֵין לוֹ'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the daughters' words cannot prove the law, the only solid source is ה׳'s own command: 'If a man dies and has no son, pass his inheritance to his daughter.' A son comes before a daughter.

keyTerms.meaning: it is clear
as we answered at first

steps.whatToRemember: The final source that a son comes before a daughter is the תורה's command 'אִישׁ כִּי יָמוּת וּבֵן אֵין לוֹ' (במדבר 27:8). It is not learned from the request of בנות צלפחד.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key rule of how the גמרא proves הלכה. What people in a story said or assumed is weaker proof than the תורה's own command.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear
as we answered at first.
phrases.notes: This points back to אביי's source from 'וּבֵן אֵין לוֹ' (במדבר 27:8).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge in step 7 and goes back to the earlier source.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A son comes before a daughter in inheritance, learned from 'וּבֵן אֵין לוֹ'. רב אחא בר יעקב's source is rejected.

steps.title: רבינא: the closer relative inherits first
steps.stepSummary: רבינא brings a new source: the פסוק says the inheritance goes to 'הַקָּרֹב אֵלָיו', so the closest relative comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: the source is from here: 'Who is next to him.' 'The closest' teaches that the closer relative comes first.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא offers a new source that a son comes before a daughter: the Torah gives the inheritance to the closest relative.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הַקָּרוֹב, 'the closest', sets up a ranking: whoever is closer to the person who died inherits first. For this to prove that a son beats a daughter, we still need to show that a son is closer than a daughter. The next step asks exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who is next to him', the closest relative
The closer relative comes first
From here, introducing a source

phrases.english: Ravina said: from here:
"Who is next to him"
"The closest": the closer one comes first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new source after the first source, 'וּבֵן אֵין לוֹ', was restored in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The closer relative inherits first ('הַקָּרוֹב'), and this is meant to place a son before a daughter.

steps.title: How is a son closer than a daughter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes a son a closer relative than a daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is it that makes a son closer than a daughter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the obvious next question about רבינא's source: in what way is a son 'closer' than a daughter?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא's proof only works if a son really counts as closer. Both are children of the father, so the closeness needs to be shown, not just assumed.

keyTerms.meaning: Closeness, how near a relative is
And what

phrases.english: And what is the closeness of a son over a daughter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the hidden assumption in רבינא's source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What shows that a son is a closer relative than a daughter?

steps.title: Suggested answer: a son takes his father's place
steps.stepSummary: The suggested answer: a son stands in his father's place for יְעִדָה and for שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה, and a daughter does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because a son stands in place of his father for designating a maidservant, and for an ancestral field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests an answer: there are two areas of הלכה where a son takes his father's place, and this shows he is closer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With יְעִדָה, a son can marry his father's Hebrew maidservant by designating her as his wife. With שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה, a son also steps into his father's role. Since a son replaces the father in these laws, the idea is that he must be 'closer'.

keyTerms.meaning: Designating a Hebrew maidservant as a wife
An ancestral field, family land handed down
Stands in place of his father

phrases.english: That a son stands in place of his father
for designation and for an ancestral field?
phrases.notes: Designation means marrying the father's Hebrew maidservant by making her his wife. A son can do this in his father's place.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁבֵּן קָם תַּחַת אָבִיו לִיעִדָה וְלִשְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a suggested answer to the question in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A son takes his father's place for יְעִדָה and for שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה, so he is closer.

steps.title: Neither example proves a son is closer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects both examples. A daughter cannot do יְעִדָה in any case, and the son's status for שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה comes from the יבום reasoning, which a daughter fits as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: Designation? A daughter is not a candidate for designation at all! An ancestral field also comes from this same refutation, because the תנא holds: is there יבום anywhere except where there is no son?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down both examples. Neither one shows that a son is closer than a daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יְעִדָה proves nothing, because a daughter obviously cannot marry a maidservant. Being able to do it is not about closeness. For שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה, the son's special status is itself learned from the rule that there is no יבום when there is a son, and a daughter also prevents יבום. So this example cannot rank a son above a daughter.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation, a weak point in an argument
Levirate marriage, a brother marrying the childless widow
He holds, it is established for him
Is not a candidate for, not subject to

steps.confusionAlert: The point is not that a daughter is less close. It is that these two examples cannot measure closeness between a son and a daughter at all.

phrases.aramaic: יְעִדָה – בַּת לָאו בַּת יְעִדָה הִיא!
phrases.english: Designation: a daughter is not subject to designation at all!
An ancestral field also:
it comes from this very same refutation,
for the תנא holds:

phrases.aramaic: כְּלוּם יֵשׁ יִבּוּם – אֶלָּא בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁאֵין בֵּן!
phrases.english: Is there יבום anywhere except where there is no son?
phrases.notes: A daughter also prevents יבום, so this reasoning puts a son and a daughter on the same level.

steps.triggerLanguage: יְעִדָה – בַּת לָאו בַּת יְעִדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggested answer from step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Both examples, יְעִדָה and שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה, are rejected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: יְעִדָה does not apply to a daughter at all. The שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה status rests on יבום logic, which covers a daughter as well.

steps.title: Back to the first source
steps.stepSummary: Since רבינא's source cannot be proven, the גמרא goes back to its original answer, 'וּבֵן אֵין לוֹ'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear that the source is as we answered at the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops רבינא's source and confirms the first source again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a way to show that a son is 'closer', 'הַקָּרֹב אֵלָיו' cannot place a son before a daughter. So the original source from step 8, 'וּבֵן אֵין לוֹ', stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is clear
As we answered at the start

steps.whatToRemember: רבינא's 'הַקָּרֹב אֵלָיו' fails because nothing shows that a son is closer than a daughter. The main source stays 'וּבֵן אֵין לוֹ'.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear: it is as we answered at the start.
phrases.notes: He means the first source, 'וּבֵן אֵין לוֹ', that the גמרא already went back to in step 8.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the rejection in step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The source that a son comes before a daughter remains 'וּבֵן אֵין לוֹ'.

steps.title: Another source: 'your sons', not your daughters
steps.stepSummary: An alternative source: the פסוק about inheriting slaves says 'לִבְנֵיכֶם', which means sons and not daughters.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say it is from here: 'And you may make them an inheritance for your sons after you.' 'Your sons', and not your daughters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another possible source that a son comes before a daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בְּנֵיכֶם is read narrowly as 'your sons', which leaves daughters out. That would show that sons are the ones who inherit, ahead of daughters.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say, introducing another answer
And you may give as an inheritance
Your sons (or your children)

phrases.english: And if you want, say: from here:
"And you may make them an inheritance
for your sons after you"
"Your sons", and not your daughters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another possible source alongside the main one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'לִבְנֵיכֶם' means sons, not daughters, so sons inherit first.

steps.title: Does the blessing of long life leave out daughters?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this reading: the same word appears in the בְּרָכָה of long days, and that surely includes daughters.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, 'So that your days and the days of your sons may be many': there too, will it mean 'your sons' and not your daughters?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the new reading against another פסוק that uses the same word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בְּנֵיכֶם always means only sons, then the promise of long life would leave out daughters. That makes no sense, so it seems בְּנֵיכֶם means 'children'.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, introducing a challenge from what follows
So that your days may be many

phrases.english: But if so,
"So that your days and the days of your sons may be many"
there too, "your sons", and not your daughters?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in step 14.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word in a בְּרָכָה clearly includes daughters, so the word must mean 'children'.

steps.title: A blessing is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a בְּרָכָה is read broadly, so there בְּנֵיכֶם includes daughters. In a law of inheritance it means sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: A blessing is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the new source by setting blessings apart from laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a בְּרָכָה, the תורה is giving good to everyone, so בְּנֵיכֶם is read broadly as 'children'. In a law of inheritance, the word keeps its narrower meaning, 'sons'. So the source from 'לִבְנֵיכֶם' still works.

keyTerms.meaning: A blessing
Is different

steps.whatToRemember: The same word can be read broadly in a בְּרָכָה and narrowly in a law. That is why 'לִבְנֵיכֶם' can still teach that sons inherit before daughters.

phrases.english: A blessing is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the two contexts (a blessing versus a law)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בְּנֵיכֶם must mean the same thing everywhere, so it includes daughters.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a בְּרָכָה, בְּנֵיכֶם includes daughters. In a law of inheritance, it means sons only.

steps.title: What is the source that paternal brothers inherit from each other?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that brothers from the same father inherit from each other, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: brothers from the same father inherit from each other and pass inheritance to each other. Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line in the משנה and asks where the rule comes from. This sets up רבה's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that paternal brothers inherit from each other. It did not say that maternal brothers (same mother, different father) do. The גמרא wants a פסוק that limits inheritance to the father's side.

keyTerms.meaning: Brothers who share the same father (paternal brothers)
They inherit and they pass on an inheritance, in both directions
"From where do we know this?" The גמרא is asking for a source

phrases.english: And the brothers from the father
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה. Brothers from the father means they share a father, even if their mothers are different.

phrases.english: inherit and bequeath, etc.
From where do we derive this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of a son coming before a daughter (steps 1-16) and opens a new line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that shows inheritance between brothers goes only through the father.

steps.title: רבה learns it from the brothers of יעקב's sons
steps.stepSummary: רבה compares the word אחוה in the inheritance פסוקים to the word אחוה used for the sons of יעקב, who were brothers only through their father.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: we learn it by comparing the word "brothers" here to the word "brothers" used for the sons of יעקב. There, it means brothers from the same father and not from the same mother. Here too, it means brothers from the same father and not from the same mother.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question with a גזירה שוה, a comparison between the same word in two places in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sons of יעקב had four different mothers, yet the תורה calls them all brothers. So "brothers" in the תורה means sharing a father. רבה carries that meaning over to the inheritance פסוק, which talks about brothers inheriting.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who gives the source
"It comes": it is learned from a comparison
Brotherhood, brothers
"Just as there, so too here": the standard wording of a גזירה שוה

phrases.english: Rabba said:
It is derived from "brothers" – "brothers" from the sons of Jacob;
phrases.notes: The two פסוקים are בראשית מב:יג (the twelve brothers) and במדבר כז:י (inheritance going to brothers).

phrases.aramaic: מַה לְהַלָּן, מִן הָאָב וְלֹא מִן הָאֵם;
phrases.english: just as there, it is from the father and not from the mother;
phrases.notes: The sons of יעקב had different mothers but one father.

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן, מִן הָאָב וְלֹא מִן הָאֵם.
phrases.english: so too here, it is from the father and not from the mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of אחוה from the sons of יעקב shows that brothers means paternal brothers.

steps.title: Why is רבה's comparison needed if משפחה already teaches it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we need רבה's גזירה שוה, since the inheritance פסוק says "from his family", and only the father's side is called family.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need this? It is written, "from his family, and he shall inherit it." The father's family is called "family", and the mother's family is not called "family"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה by pointing out that another פסוק already teaches the same rule, so his comparison seems unneeded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inheritance פסוק says the inheritance goes to a relative "from his family." In the תורה, משפחה means the father's side only. So it is already clear that all inheritance goes through the father, which makes רבה's גזירה שוה seem extra.

keyTerms.meaning: "Why do I need it?" The גמרא is asking why a source is needed
Family. In the תורה it means the father's side
The father's family
The mother's family

phrases.english: But why do I need this?
It is written: "Of his family, and he shall inherit it" –
the father's family is called "family,"
the mother's family is not called "family"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רבה's source in step 18 is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's גזירה שוה from the sons of יעקב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word ממשפחתו already limits all inheritance to the father's side, so a separate source for brothers is unneeded.

steps.title: רבה's teaching was really about יבום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that for inheritance the comparison is not needed, and explains that רבה said it about יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true. And when רבה's teaching was said, it was said about יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge and moves רבה's teaching to a different topic, יבום, where it is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For inheritance, משפחה is enough. But the יבום פסוקים also speak of "brothers", and the word משפחה does not appear there. So רבה's comparison teaches that only a brother from the same father does יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: "Yes, it is indeed so." The גמרא agrees with the question
It was said
Marrying the widow of a brother who died without children

steps.whatToRemember: Inheritance goes only through the father's side, learned from the word משפחה. רבה's comparison to the sons of יעקב teaches that יבום is only done by a paternal brother.

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so;
phrases.notes: The גמרא agrees that for inheritance, רבה's comparison really isn't needed.

phrases.english: and when Rabba's statement was said,
it was said with regard to levirate marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19 by agreeing and moving רבה's statement to a different topic.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Agreement plus reassigning the statement to a different topic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבה's גזירה שוה was meant as the source for inheritance between brothers.
steps.terutzMaskana: Inheritance is learned from ממשפחתו; רבה's גזירה שוה teaches that יבום applies only to paternal brothers.

steps.title: What is the source that a man inherits his mother?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, about a man and his mother, asks for its source, and begins to bring a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: a man inherits his mother, etc. Where do these things come from? As the רבנן taught:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new line of the משנה and asks for its source. It then begins to quote a ברייתא, which is the answer that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a setup step. The question is asked here, and the words "as the רבנן taught" introduce the ברייתא that will give the source in the coming lines.

keyTerms.meaning: A man and his mother: the משנה's case of a son inheriting his mother

"As the רבנן taught": introduces a ברייתא
